name: github.run.logs
description: Read a bounded excerpt of one GitHub Actions run's logs — failed steps by default, or the full log — plus runner checkout evidence. Optionally scope the excerpt to a named step (step, usually with job) or to a byte window (byte_start/byte_end, 0-based end-exclusive) or line window (line_start/line_end, 1-based end-exclusive); a window combined with step applies within the step section, an absent step or window fails without returning other log bytes, and the response reports the selection and its selected_bytes/selected_lines. In a raw job log, steps are named only by their `Run <command>` display group, which closes before the command runs, so a step matched there includes its post-group runtime output until the next `Run` step; a workflow step name that differs from its `Run` command cannot be reliably mapped in a raw log and fails with an explicit unsupported-mapping error instead of a not-found error. The source stream is read incrementally with an 8 MiB stdout limit and process timeout. A separate diagnostic_unit retains a unique complete failing runner command up to 256 KiB; display truncation does not imply missing command evidence. Source-limit exhaustion is retryable. When the run-scoped read succeeds with no output, or GitHub says the parent run is still in progress, the excerpt can be recovered from the log API of a verified completed job belonging to that run; failed scope is restricted to unsuccessful jobs. `source` and `source_jobs` identify the recovery. Other errors remain errors.

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: Numeric workflow-run ID

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: Numeric job ID to narrow the log to one job

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: "failed" (default) for failed-step logs, or "all" for the full run log — use "all" to evidence the checked-out commit, since the checkout step usually succeeds

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Maximum head/tail excerpt bytes (default 16384, capped at 262144), plus omission markers and up to 64 KiB of nextest failure blocks (16 KiB per block, at most 128 blocks). failure_regions includes original byte ranges; selection_complete is false if the scan or block-count limit is reached. The separate complete diagnostic_unit is capped at 262144 bytes.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Repository in owner/name format (uses current directory if omitted)

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Exact workflow step name to return only that step's log section (usually with job); fails if the step is absent, or with an unsupported-mapping error when a raw job log names the step only by a differing `Run <command>`

parameters.name: byte_start
parameters.description: Start of a byte window (0-based, inclusive); with byte_end returns exactly those bytes, bounded by max_bytes

parameters.name: byte_end
parameters.description: End of a byte window (0-based, exclusive); must be greater than byte_start

parameters.name: line_start
parameters.description: Start of a line window (1-based, inclusive); with line_end returns exactly those lines, bounded by max_bytes

parameters.name: line_end
parameters.description: End of a line window (1-based, exclusive); must be greater than line_start

parameters.name: until

name: orbit.command.exec
description: Execute a command as an explicit argv array in an explicit working directory and return its stdout, stderr, and exit status, within a deadline. The child receives an allowlisted environment: baseline process context, git author and committer identity, and Orbit's execution envelope.

parameters.name: argv

parameters.name: working_directory

parameters.name: timeout_ms

parameters.name: claim_token

parameters.description: For list: Only requests on this task; For raise: The human-crew task this decision concerns.

name: orbit.decision.digest
description: Raise the approval decision requests a decision channel's digest presents, and return the whole digest in one call. Callable only by the plugin the channel is bound to, through its callback session, or by the operator, never by an agent session. Repeated calls reuse requests for unchanged task bindings; newly eligible tasks can add requests. With the decision channel disabled, it returns no requests. The binding rules and result fields are in the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Decision requests`.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The registered decision channel the digest is for, as `orbit decision channel list` shows it.

name: orbit.decision.submit
description: Submit a human's answer to one open decision request through a registered decision channel. Callable only by the plugin the channel is bound to, through its callback session, or by the operator testing the channel, never by an agent session. Core verifies the channel, the request's binding, the answer and the single-use token, and checks a forwarded raw message's DKIM signature itself. A refusal returns its error code and applies nothing. The refusal codes, DKIM rules and retry behaviour are in the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Decision requests`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The decision request id, as action `list` prints it.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The registered decision channel submitting the answer, as `orbit decision channel list` shows it.

parameters.name: answer
parameters.description: The human's chosen answer id, one of the request's allowed answers. An empty answer is refused as unparseable.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The per-request single-use token minted for this request under the channel key. Core verifies it; presenting it never reveals it back.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Evidence or note kept with the answer. A pilot-admission `evaluated` answer uses it as its evidence and is refused without one.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: The transport sender the submission presents as evidence. A plugin submission must present one; when the channel has a sender allowlist, the sender must be on it. The operator's own test submission may omit it.

parameters.name: auth_results
parameters.description: The raw Authentication-Results header the transport forwards as evidence. A plugin submission must forward one: core requires dkim=pass and spf=pass and refuses on dmarc=fail. The operator's own test submission may omit it.

parameters.name: raw_message
parameters.description: The raw reply message the transport forwards for core-side DKIM verification, at most 262144 bytes (256 KiB). When present, core verifies the message's DKIM signature itself and refuses when its result contradicts the forwarded verdicts. Required on a channel registered with require_dkim_verification; optional otherwise.

name: orbit.drain.claim.bind
description: Bind an executor's local leaf run to its execution claim on the owner, moving the claim from `claimed` to `running`. Idempotent: repeating the same run returns the recorded outcome, and a different run is refused, so one claim never has two leaves. The owner fences the claim against the session's own machine; a claim admitted to another machine, or already settled or revoked, is refused as stale.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The claim `orbit.task.pull` admitted to this machine.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The one local leaf run the executor created for this claim.

parameters.name: ship
parameters.description: The ship contract the claim was admitted under, from its receipt.

name: orbit.drain.claim.effort
description: Report, after the fact, the reasoning effort and implementing model a claimed leaf ran at when its settlement carried none, so the owner's agent scorecards stop counting the attempt as effort unknown or model unknown. Accepted only from the machine that ran the claim, for the leaf run bound to it, once the claim is settled; a claim that settled before the owner kept settlement records is accepted only when the task's history names it as pulled. Attribution only: it changes no claim, task, run or settlement outcome. A value the claim already holds is never overwritten: the same value replays, and a different one is refused as `effort_conflict` or `model_conflict`, recording neither.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The settled claim whose leaf ran on this machine.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The leaf run bound to that claim.

parameters.name: reasoning_effort
parameters.description: The effective reasoning effort of the leaf's main implementing invocation, read from this machine's own records: its name (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`), or `provider_default` when the provider's default applied. Never sent for an unknown effort.

parameters.name: crew_model
parameters.description: The model of that same implementing invocation (else of its latest matching launch record), read from this machine's own records. Omitted when unknown; never derived from a crew name or configuration.

parameters.name: crew
parameters.description: The crew the leaf run actually used, read from this machine's own run record. Sent with the same report as `crew_model`, so the owner keys the attempt to this crew and model together when the task was re-crewed between claims. Omitted when unknown; an owner that predates it ignores the field.

name: orbit.drain.claim.settle
description: Settle an execution claim on the owner. A typed handoff is accepted only after the owner reads the pull request from the provider and resolves its candidate and base in the owner's own checkout, and only with digest-pinned validation evidence; it moves the task to `review`, which awaits owner approval — it does not merge. A failure records its evidence and blocks the task. A release (a cancelled drain giving back work it will not finish) returns the task to the backlog with its reason as a comment. Each releases only this claim's reservation. Retries replay the recorded outcome.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The claim being settled.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The leaf run bound to this claim, when one was bound.

parameters.name: settlement
parameters.description: The executor's durable settlement: `{"AcceptHandoff": <typed handoff>}` for a published pull request, `{"Fail": <evidence>}`, or `{"Release": <evidence>}` to hand an unfinished claim back. Nothing else settles a claim.

parameters.name: crew
parameters.description: Optional. The crew the leaf run resolved. Attribution only: the owner records it on the claim's settlement record, after any crew the settlement's own evidence names, and never uses it to validate or decide the settlement.

parameters.name: crew_model
parameters.description: Optional. The model the leaf's crew resolved to. Attribution only, like `crew`.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Optional. The branch the leaf run's worktree recorded. Attribution only, like `crew`; the owner shows it so an operator can inspect the run.

parameters.name: worktree_path
parameters.description: Optional. The absolute path of the leaf run's worktree on the executing machine. Attribution only, like `branch`.

parameters.name: reasoning_effort
parameters.description: Optional. The effective reasoning effort of the leaf's main implementing invocation: its name (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`), or `provider_default` when the provider's default applied. Omit it when the effort is unknown. Attribution only, like `crew`: the owner's agent scorecards count the attempt under it.

name: orbit.drain.claims
description: List this workspace's execution claims for inspection and deliberate recovery: phase, age, reservation expiry, execution machine, bound run, last recorded event, unresolved merge intent, and landing invalidation. Age, an expired reservation, and an absent local run are diagnostics, not proof that a worker died — nothing here reclaims, rebinds, or repairs a claim.

name: orbit.drain.probe
description: Read-only preflight for the distributed drain, served by the workspace owner. Reports the owner machine, binary version, distributed-drain protocol schema, the capabilities this session holds, the diagnostic caller machine, the owner-resolved ship configuration, and both review switches (`review.timing` and the after-landing auto-task). Declaring `caller_version`, `caller_schema`, or `caller_before_pr` also reports the first refusal an admission would raise, in the order admission applies it. It creates no request receipt, reservation, claim, or task transition, and it is never a health check for admission itself.

parameters.name: caller_version
parameters.description: Optional. The calling binary's version. When supplied, the response reports whether it matches this owner instead of leaving the caller to compare.

parameters.name: caller_schema
parameters.description: Optional. The caller's distributed-drain wire-protocol schema version. This is not the MCP protocol revision and not the orchestration schema version.

parameters.name: caller_fingerprint
parameters.description: Optional. Type-derived pull request schema fingerprint. Discover the owner's protocol_fingerprint before declaring this field; a mismatch raises protocol_skew before any pull.

parameters.name: caller_before_pr
parameters.description: Optional. Whether the executor's `review.timing` is `before_pr`. Diagnostic only: a claimed leaf runs the before-PR review the owner's ship contract captures, never the executor's own. After-landing review never affects admission.

name: orbit.drain.receipt.lookup
description: Read-only reconciliation of one distributed-drain admission request, served by the workspace owner. Returns the original receipt and the current claim phase (`found`), a non-reusable tombstone (`expired`), or `not_found`. It creates no receipt, binds no run, and grants no execution authority: a receipt is historical evidence, and `not_found` is not proof that an earlier request cannot still arrive, so it never licenses a replacement request under a new ID.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The durable request ID the original admission was made with. It is read verbatim; the stored receipt is never rewritten to match the caller's current binary.

parameters.name: machine_id
parameters.description: Optional receipt namespace: the machine the original request was made from. Defaults to this session's own machine. Naming another machine is cross-attempt inspection and requires operator capability.

parameters.name: lookup_schema

parameters.description: Memory key: the model id a space belongs to, as runs record it, or `global`.

name: orbit.memory.propose
description: Propose a note for the global memory every model receives, for an operator to accept or reject. Only a crew memory dreaming task's run may propose, at most 2 proposals per run. The note is refused, naming the rule, when it breaks the global memory's caps (3 KiB), provenance (at least one evidence task id, each from the run's evidence pack), the score-blind lint or the not-instructions lint. Refused while crew_memory.enabled is false.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The proposed global-memory note, at most 3 KiB of Markdown. It passes the same rules as a global-memory write.

parameters.name: evidence

name: orbit.memory.show
description: Show a crew memory space: the files of its newest revision (or of `revision`), their digest and size, the evidence the write cited, its writer and reason. Without key, summarise every space: while crew_memory.enabled is set, `global`, each key with a revision, and each configured or proposing key with none yet; while it is false, only the spaces with a stored revision. A key with no revision shows an empty space. Read only; works whether or not crew_memory.enabled is set. An agent may call it only from a run: a crew memory dreaming task's run or a run in a memory experiment arm reads only its own model's space (the default key) or `global`, and the run of a task whose `granted_tools` an operator set to include this tool reads any space, any revision and the summary.

An agent may write only from a crew memory dreaming task's run, and only that task's own key: another model's key and `global` are refused (propose a global note instead).

Closing a notice that is already closed or expired returns it unchanged with already_inactive: true.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The notice id, as orbit.notice.list prints it. Give id or dedupe_key, not both.

parameters.name: dedupe_key
parameters.description: Close the open notice holding this key in the home workspace.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why the notice no longer applies, 1-240 characters.

parameters.name: orchestrator

name: orbit.notice.list

With a workspace, that workspace's notices plus global notices homed elsewhere on its owner; with all: true, every workspace homed on this owner; without a workspace in a federated session, every reachable owner's notices merged, deduplicated by id and limited once after the merge. Each notice carries its kind, scope, title, body, author class, linked task and its status, expiry, report count and effective status (open, closed or expired, derived when read). Ordered incident, maintenance, info, newest update first. Output {notices, degraded}; degraded names any owner or home that could not be read, so a shorter list never silently hides an unreachable owner. Read-only.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: List notices from every workspace homed on this owner, not only the selected one. Without a limit, every match is returned.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Effective state: open (the default), closed, expired or all. Closed and expired notices stay listable for the retention window.

parameters.name: include_global
parameters.description: Also return global notices homed in other workspaces on this owner (default true).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Only workspace or only global notices.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only these kinds.

parameters.name: linked_task
parameters.description: Only notices linked to this task.

parameters.name: author_class
parameters.description: Only notices posted by operator, orchestrator or agent.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Only maintenance notices whose hosts include this machine id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many notices, 1-200 (default 50).

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.notice.post
description: Post a fleet notice: a short, scoped note every agent and operator in its scope should see until it stops being true (an incident, planned maintenance, or other information). Not a lease notice: lease notices are events on one path lease. The notice is held by this workspace's owner, expires (defaults by kind, capped by poster class), closes when its linked task is done, and is deduplicated by dedupe_key: posting a key an open notice already holds updates it when you may edit it, or corroborates it (bumps its report count) when you may not. The response is {notice, outcome} with outcome created, updated or corroborated; a lost reply is safe to retry. Who you post as (operator, orchestrator or agent) comes from your session, never from input; a managed agent may post only incident or info notices about its own workspace, for at most 24 hours, with a linked task or evidence. A notice informs; it grants nothing.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: incident (something is broken now), maintenance (planned work others should hold off or plan around) or info (anything else worth knowing).

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: One line, 1-120 characters, no control characters.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Plain text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; Markdown is stored verbatim and never rendered as HTML.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: workspace (the home workspace only, the default) or global (every workspace whose readers reach this owner).

parameters.name: dedupe_key
parameters.description: Subject key, 1-128 characters of a-z 0-9 . _ : / -. Defaults to task:<linked_task> or <kind>:<title slug>. Posting a key an open notice holds updates or corroborates that notice instead of opening a second one.

parameters.name: linked_task
parameters.description: Id of the task the notice is about, usually its fix. It must be a task this workspace's owner holds, in this or another of its workspaces. When that task is done the notice closes, unless close_on_linked_done is false.

parameters.name: close_on_linked_done
parameters.description: Close the notice when its linked task is done. Defaults to true with linked_task.

parameters.name: evidence

parameters.name: hosts
parameters.description: Up to 32 machine ids a maintenance notice concerns. Refused on other kinds.

parameters.name: expires_in_hours
parameters.description: Hours until the notice expires. Defaults by kind (incident 72, maintenance 12, info 168); capped by poster class, and a longer request is refused rather than clamped. Mutually exclusive with expires_at.

parameters.name: expires_at
parameters.description: RFC 3339 instant the notice expires, at least 5 minutes ahead. Mutually exclusive with expires_in_hours.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it never outranks the operator or a managed run's binding.

name: orbit.resident.checkpoint

name: orbit.resident.control
description: Control a resident mandate's firing: pause, resume, stop, wake (status_request makes the cycle checkpoint even when idle), takeover or release. Each action is a history entry with the caller and reason. Pause, stop and takeover start no new cycle; a live cycle keeps its frozen grant, checkpoints and exits at its boundary. Stop ends the mandate and moves the assignment to review once no cycle is live. Resume and release restore firing under the existing authority and never widen it. Any caller that can write the assignment may call it. Output {task_id, action, state, effective_at}.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: pause (active to paused: no new cycle), resume (paused to active), stop (ends the mandate: no new cycle, then the assignment moves to review), wake (active: due on the next tick despite the heartbeat, never the cadence floor), takeover (active or paused to taken_over: no cycle fires) or release (taken_over to active).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why, recorded in the assignment's history with the caller.

parameters.name: status_request
parameters.description: With wake: the cycle writes a checkpoint even when it has nothing else to do.

parameters.name: by_session
parameters.description: The session taking over or acting, recorded with the action.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

Read-only. Defaults to 14d and the top 5 pains.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start as a span (7d, 24h, 2w) or RFC 3339 instant; defaults to the configured evolution window.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Maximum pains to return, 1-100; default 5.

parameters.name: orchestrator
parameters.description: Orchestrator crew for this unmanaged session. Defaults to the session's configured orchestrator. Attribution only: it is recorded on a grant request as the relaying session and never grants authority.

name: orbit.resident.grant
description: Widen or narrow a resident mandate's authority: its rights (dispatch, promote, merge, plugin_upgrade) and covered workspaces. Widening (add, workspaces) is the human's: from an operator it applies at once; from any other caller it changes nothing and raises one resident_authority decision request that quotes `quote` verbatim and names your session, and the authority changes only if a human answers grant. An open request for the same addition is returned, not duplicated; any authority change supersedes it. Narrowing (remove, drop_workspaces, a shorter deadline) applies at once for any caller that can write the assignment and is recorded with that caller. A call may not widen and narrow at once. Output {outcome, authority, request?} with outcome granted, requested or narrowed.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The mandate's assignment task: a task tagged `resident` carrying a resident/mandate.json artifact.

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Rights to add: dispatch, promote, merge or plugin_upgrade. Widening.

parameters.name: workspaces
parameters.description: Workspaces to add to the authority's scope; each must be one the mandate lists. Widening.

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: For auto: Start only: add this review layer before landing (before-landing recommended; before-pr deprecated but honoured) to the window when workspace policy applies none; every task it admits inherits it; For ship: Optional review layer before landing (`before-landing` recommended; `before-pr` deprecated but honoured) this run adds when workspace policy applies none.

parameters.name: approve_proposed
parameters.description: For auto: Start only: each pass pilots qualifying proposed tasks (tagged no-diff-expected, or with context_files and an assessed complexity) and approves into backlog those with no duplicate, already-landed, conflict or warning finding, including tasks filed during the window.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: For auto: Stop only: also cancel each live drain and stop its in-flight work.

parameters.name: claim_token
parameters.description: For auto: Workspace claim token when held by another operator; For ship: Token for this workspace's exclusive claim, required when another operator holds one.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Exact selector returned by workspace discovery. No implicit destination.

parameters.name: task_ids
parameters.description: For ship: Explicit task IDs to ship; at least one is required.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: For ship: Optional base branch override.

parameters.name: allowed_crews
parameters.description: For ship: Optional configured crews this explicit shipment may dispatch; excluded crews are rejected before provider invocation.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: For land: The task in review whose delivery pull request lands.

name: proc.spawn
description: Spawn a process with timeout and capture output. The timeout ceiling is 60000 ms outside a managed activity; inside one it is the activity's remaining wall-clock budget, at most 45 min

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: Program to execute

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Arguments to pass to the program

parameters.name: timeout_ms
parameters.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds (default 15000). Larger values are clamped to the effective ceiling, which the result reports as timeout_ceiling_ms: 60000 outside a managed activity, or the smaller of the activity's remaining budget and 45 min inside one
